newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker in tight ranges.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker in tight ranges.

text.p: London's August white sugar contract moved marginally lower on Friday morning and accounted for nearly all of the light overall volume.
Traders said the spot position was deriving most of its recent support from Russian purchases of European white sugar, in addition to the expected hefty arrivals of Brazilian and Cuban raws.
At 1200 GMT August was down 40 cents at $317.60 while October was 70 cents lower at $307.00. Overall volume was 355 lots and ranges were tight at a maximum 30 cents.
"The August is still going on the back of supposed Russian interest...but there's starting to be some support even further down the board," said one trader.
He noted increased end-user interest at lower levels.
Market sources said what was suspected to be fund buyers were keeping August/October above $10 while there was scale-up producer selling in both August and October.
Speculators, normally more prevalent on the New York market, are also believed to have moved into August.
Traders said the unknown size of the spec position could cause August/October to widen towards expiry and then collapse during the bale-out in the last few dats.
Activity is expected to be mostly subdued into next week as players start to gather in New York for the Sugar Dinner on Wednesday.
Trading in Paris was confined to 241 lots of the August contract, which was down $1.00 at $317.50.
